answer: Before dawn on the tundra, the ground holds its breath. I walk in the half-dark, boots crunching frost, until the sky begins to lean. First light slides across the flat land and turns every ripple of moss into a dune in miniature. The horizon there is so wide it feels patient, as if it has been waiting for someone to look at it properly. I do, for a long minute. Then I turn back, and my tracks behind me are already fading, and I find I don't mind at all.
